name: Wicklow Way
description_md:
The Wicklow Way is a 128.2 km waymarked hiking route located in IE. This national waymarked hiking network trail is signposted as WW and is classified as hard due to the distance and 4077 m of ascent.

The route involves 4105 m of descent and requires about 43 hours on the DIN 33466 hiking time rule. It passes Glendalough within 100 m, the Glendalough Round Tower within 200 m, and the Glendalough Cathedral within 300 m.

images.title: White Hill, Wicklow, Ireland.jpg
images.author: Rob Hurson
images.caption: This was taken on White Hill. The three hills in the middle ground are Scarr (Scor / "Sharp Rock"), Knocknacloghoge (Cnoc na Clochóige / "Hill with Stony Bits") and Luggala (Log an Lágh / "Hollow of the Hill"). The Turlough Hill pumped hydro station is silhouetted straight ahead,

images.title: Wicklow Way Conifer Plantation.jpg
images.author: Joe King
images.caption: Forest road through a conifer plantation on the Wicklow Way National Waymarked Trail in Glencullen Forest, County Dublin, Ireland. The National Waymarked Trails in Ireland are often criticised for their monotonous paths through state-owned forestry plantations

images.title: Wicklow Way Clonegal Trailhead.jpg
images.author: Joe King
images.caption: The trailhead of the Wicklow Way in Clonegal, County Carlow, Ireland. The Wicklow Way is a 132km long-distance National Waymarked Trail that runs from Marlay Park in County Dublin across County Wicklow and ends at Clonegal in County Carlow. The trailhead is denoted by a map board
